title: A pilot study on the effects of tactile emotion transmission in video-based psychotherapy for unipolar depression
summary:
Numerous studies show that the quality of the relationship between the therapist and the patient has a significant influence on the course and outcome of psychotherapeutic treatment. Shaping the relationship in online/video therapy poses particular challenges. Therapists often observe that video therapy has disadvantages for the therapeutic alliance due to the lack of important physical signals. The lack of such information could therefore impair communication between the therapist and the patient. In addition, patients in psychotherapy often do not feel able to express their emotional states and negative reactions to the therapist's approach. This often reduces the patient's co-operation. To solve these problems, a technical system for the intuitive exchange of information about emotional states is used in video therapy. This addition to the communication between therapist and patient is intended to support the relationship. 
This clinical pilot study examines whether positive effects on symptom reduction and the quality of the therapeutic relationship can be achieved through the transmission of emotions by touch stimuli via such a technical system in video-based psychotherapy for depression.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with a diagnosis of unipolar depression (ICD F32.1, F32.2, F33.1, F33.2) who can be treated with video therapy in an outpatient setting based on the assessment of the clinical pre-diagnosis.
Exclusion criteria:
Presence of chronic depression, i.e. the existence of depressive symptoms for more than two years continuously.
Exclusion criteria are also the presence of a current diagnosis from the area of addiction disorders (ICD10 F1x), a mental illness due to an experienced brain injury or neurodegenerative disease (F0x) and the presence of a schizophrenic disorder (F2x).
